He strongly agrees Judeo-Christian values provide the necessary moral framework for limited government. — best matches stance 5 (strongly protect religious freedom and allow religious organizations complete autonomy in their operations and hiring practices).

He strongly disagrees with adding gender identity as a protected class (iVoterGuide). His 2023 vote for HB209 clearly shows he supports restricting transgender athletes to teams matching biological sex. — best matches stance 4 (require transgender athletes to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth).

No evidence of support for environmental restrictions on fossil fuel development. — best matches stance 5 (remove environmental restrictions and maximize fossil fuel extraction).

Grover served as Senate floor sponsor of HB261 (Equal Opportunity Initiatives, 2024), the anti-DEI bill that banned diversity/equity/inclusion trainings, programs, and offices at public institutions. iVoterGuide: strongly disagrees with CRT and with adding gender identity as a protected class; strongly disagrees with race-based reparations. — best matches stance 5 (eliminate affirmative action and all race-based government programs).

Voted in the Senate Education Committee 7-2 to advance HB215 (Utah Fits All Scholarship, 2023), which provides $8,000 scholarships for any family to use at private/religious schools. iVoterGuide: strongly agrees with vouchers, tax credits, charter schools, and homeschooling. — best matches stance 5 (providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family).

iVoterGuide 2022 survey: Grover strongly agrees the U.S. should physically secure the southern border and supports continuing the border wall. He supports those 'appropriately screened' through proper legal proceedings. This supports stricter legal entry standards and border enforcement but does not call for stopping most legal immigration. — best matches stance 4 (make it harder to immigrate legally and limit public services to people with legal status).

iVoterGuide 2022 survey: Grover selected 'Tax-payer funded health care should be abolished in all forms, and Medicaid and Medicare should be de-funded.' He also opposes vaccine mandates under any circumstances. His 2026 co-sponsorship of HB15 (Medicaid Amendments) addresses contingency triggers if federal matching funds are reduced, consistent with a preference for reducing government healthcare. — best matches stance 5 (stay out of healthcare entirely and let private markets handle all coverage decisions).

iVoterGuide 2022 survey: Grover calls for 'greater efficiency' in the tax code and states that since Utah has a surplus, 'spending should not increase and unneeded tax dollars should be returned to the taxpayer.' He sponsored SB236 (2026 Property Tax Exemption Process Amendments). Favors returning surplus to taxpayers rather than expanding spending, consistent with cutting taxes and scaling back government. — best matches stance 4 (cut taxes for everyone and scale back public services to match).

Grover voted YES on SB332 (Artificial Intelligence Revisions, 2025), which extended Utah's AI Policy Act until 2027 and maintained state-level AI oversight infrastructure. Utah's AI laws (SB226, SB332, HB452) require consumer disclosures, impose requirements on AI companies, and create accountability frameworks — he voted to extend these. This is lighter regulation than mandating safety testing but more than pure voluntary guidelines. — best matches stance 2 (suggest AI safety guidelines but let companies choose whether to follow them). Note: Utah's approach is somewhat between 2 and 3; 2 is the closest fit given the light-touch, pro-industry orientation.
